asset_explanations.caption: Figure 1: Example of our long trajectory for knowledge-intensive scenarios (Top) and optimization comparison of multi-agent frameworks (Bottom). Solid and dashed arrows indicate inference and optimization paths, respectively.
asset_explanations.summary: The figure illustrates a multi-agent framework for knowledge-intensive tasks, divided into two main sections. The top section depicts a workflow trajectory starting from a task instruction, moving through intent reconstruction and knowledge access, then to fact identification and relevance discrimination, finally producing a response with citations. The bottom section compares three optimization strategies for this framework: (a) Modular Optimization, (b) End-to-end Optimization, and (c) the proposed 'Our Optimization' method, using robot icons and arrows to denote agent interactions and optimization paths.

asset_explanations.caption: Figure 2: Overview of our multi-agent framework with long- and short-trajectory learning. This framework incorporates four agents: intent reconstructor, knowledge retriever, fac locator, and response generator.

asset_explanations.caption: Figure 3: Overview of Long-Short Trajectory Learning. It consists of two stages, for short trajectory learning, under a given trajectory head, requires insight into the various explicit and implicit signals in each particular task. For long-trajectory learning, LLM executes the entire process by predicting different trajectory tokens, ensuring the synergism of different short-trajectories.
asset_explanations.summary: The figure illustrates a 'Long-Short Trajectory Learning' framework, contrasting short trajectory learning (top section) with long-trajectory learning (bottom section). The top section displays three distinct modules—Intent Reconstructor, Fact Locator, and Response Generator—each processing specific tokens. The bottom section shows how these individual components are combined into a single, continuous sequence of tokens for long-trajectory learning, connected by colored arrows indicating the mapping between short and long trajectories.

asset_explanations.caption: Table 2: Comparison results against knowledge internalization and knowledge enhancement methods. * denotes the method we reproduce based on the same base. * denotes re-implemented methods based on the same initial model. The  $ \underline{\text{bold}} $ numbers represent the best results and the  $ \underline{\text{underlined}} $ numbers represent the second.
asset_explanations.summary: Table 2 compares knowledge internalization and knowledge enhancement methods across multiple tasks (Health, ARC-C, PopQA, Squad1, ASQA) using metrics Acc, Str_EM, R-L, and Mauve. It reports the performance of various baselines and the proposed SMART method, with best results bold and second underlined. SMART achieves the highest scores on Health Acc (73.18), PopQA Acc (42.60), ASQA Str_EM (41.16), ASQA R-L (40.66), and ASQA Mauve (91.47) among all methods, but is not the best on ARC-C or Squad1.

asset_explanations.caption: Table 3: Training Ablation and inference ablation for the contribution of different agents. L and S denote long-trajectory and short-trajectory learning, respectively. w/o $ \mathcal{A}_{f} $, w/o $ \mathcal{A}_{i} $, and w/o All denote no fact Locator, no intent reconstructor, and only response generator.
asset_explanations.summary: This table presents training and inference ablation results for the SMART model on four metrics (Health, ARC-C, Pop, AS), comparing the full model against variants without the fact locator (w/o A_f), without the intent reconstructor (w/o A_i), and without both (w/o All). Training ablation uses only long-trajectory learning (L), while inference ablation uses both long and short trajectories (L+S). The results show that each component contributes to performance, with the full model achieving the highest scores in both settings.

supported_claims.claim: In training ablation, removing the fact locator (w/o A_f) reduces Health accuracy from 72.15% to 70.13%.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Row 'SMART (L)' vs 'w/o $\mathcal{A}_{f}$' in column 'Health (Acc)' of training ablation section.

supported_claims.claim: In inference ablation, the full SMART (L+S) achieves 73.18% on Health, 65.58% on ARC-C, 42.60% on Pop, and 41.16% on AS.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Row 'SMART (L+S)' in inference ablation section across all four metric columns.

supported_claims.claim: Removing both components (w/o All) in training ablation causes a larger drop than removing either individually, e.g., Health drops from 72.15% to 57.95%.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Comparison of 'SMART (L)' row with 'w/o All' row in training ablation for Health (Acc).

supported_claims.claim: In inference ablation, removing the fact locator reduces ARC-C accuracy from 65.58% to 62.45%.
supported_claims.evidence_basis: Row 'SMART (L+S)' vs 'w/o $\mathcal{A}_{f}$' in column 'ARC-C (Acc)' of inference ablation section.

possible_misreadings.claim: The fact locator is more important than the intent reconstructor because removing the fact locator always causes a larger performance drop than removing the intent reconstructor.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: While w/o A_f often shows a larger drop than w/o A_i, the relative importance varies by metric and ablation setting. For example, in inference ablation on Pop, w/o A_f drops to 37.45% while w/o A_i drops to 39.88% (smaller drop), but the difference is not universally consistent across all metrics (e.g., on Health, both drops are similar: 71.63 vs 71.22). The table does not provide statistical significance.

possible_misreadings.claim: Using both long and short trajectories (L+S) is always better than using only long trajectories (L) for every metric.
possible_misreadings.why_wrong: The table only compares training ablation (L) with inference ablation (L+S) but these are different experimental settings (training vs. inference). The results are not directly comparable because the training ablation uses a different training procedure; it is not an ablation of the trajectory length at inference time. The improvement in inference ablation could be due to the addition of short-trajectory data during inference, but the table does not control for other factors.

limitations: The table only reports results on four specific metrics (Health, ARC-C, Pop, AS) and may not generalize to other datasets or evaluation measures.
The ablation experiments are conducted under two different regimes (training and inference), and comparisons across regimes are not valid without further controls.
The table does not provide statistical significance or confidence intervals, so the magnitude of differences may not be reliable.
The caption mentions 'w/o All' denotes only response generator, but it is unclear what baseline components are included in that condition (e.g., whether any other modules remain).

asset_explanations.caption: Table 4: Ablation studies of long-trajectory (Long) and short-trajectory (Short) learning.
asset_explanations.summary: Table 4 reports ablation study results comparing four methods (Vanilla LLM, +Short, +Long, +Short & Long) on four metrics: Health accuracy, PopQA accuracy, ASQA exact match, and ASQA ROUGE-L. The results show that the combination of short and long trajectory learning (+Short & Long) achieves the highest scores on all metrics, with values 73.18, 42.60, 41.16, and 40.66 respectively.

asset_explanations.caption: Figure 4: Effects of long-trajectory training data size (K) on three tasks, ARC-C, PopQA and ASQA.
asset_explanations.summary: The figure consists of three line charts (likely panels a, b, and c corresponding to tasks ARC-C, PopQA, and ASQA) that illustrate the effect of increasing long-trajectory training data size (K) on model performance. Each chart plots a performance metric (accuracy 'acc' or exact match 'em') on the y-axis against the number of training samples in thousands ('Num of training(k)') on the x-axis. A solid green line with markers represents the primary method's performance at different data sizes (0, 20, 60, 120, 140k), while horizontal dashed lines represent fixed baseline performances for 'SelfRag-7B' (blue) and 'MMAgent' (orange).
